title: O4 PR 4a: a track's steps fire on the exact tick for every speed multiplier
zone: crates/octocore (src/steps.rs new, src/engine.rs, src/lib.rs, tests/o4_steps.rs), tests/conformance/AMBIGUITIES.md, harness/baseline.txt (via cargo xtask baseline), handoffs/evidence, journal, specs/SPEC-0001/README.md
why_risk: the only behaviour change is for speed multipliers other than x1, which no host or panel can set today (release plan section 1, row R). Every golden is byte-identical; the guards G1 to G5 are unchanged and pass.
spec_rev: SPEC-0001 r3, release plan revision 2, sections 2.7 and 4 (R1)
evidence: handoffs/evidence/o4-4a-red.txt: before the change, 49 of 159 reduced multipliers up to 16 (and 32 of 169 at the extremes of the u8 fields) fire a step one tick late through the real engine within 20,000 ticks; on a stub keeping the f32 rule the accumulator tests fail 5 of 10.

After the change: all pass. The exact rule (k-th step on tick ceil(k*12*den/num)) holds for all 65,025 u8 pairs over two periods, the phase is n*num mod (12*den) and bounded (R1b), a clock started at the phase of tick 10^12 or 2^40 behaves the same (R1c), 159 multipliers stay exact for 10^6 ticks in the normal run and 10^7 in the ignored soak (3.2 s in release), and a multiplier change loses less than one unit of phase (R1e).

handoffs/evidence/o4-4a-mutants.txt: 13 of 14 breakages caught; SM8 is equivalent. The run found that the existing hyperstep test cannot tell a 96-tick step from a 192-tick one; engine::tests::hyperstep_linked_track_fires_on_exactly_ticks_192_384_and_576 was added (it passes on the parent commit, so it is a guard, not a change).
cargo xtask baseline: 13 tests added, none removed. Goldens: byte-identical (they only use x1).

Correction to my own earlier record: 'the first note sounds at tick 11' is not unexplained. tests/conformance/AMBIGUITIES.md already says why (the phase starts at 0 and a 12-tick step starts on the 12th tick); the guard's comment and the PR #14 description said 'unexplained' and are corrected.
unresolved: Two behaviours differ from the f32 code and are deliberate: a zero numerator never fires a step (the f32 code clamped to 1e-6, a 12-million-tick step, about 9 hours at 120 BPM), and the exactness is the point. Track::multiplier() (f32) is no longer used by the engine and stays as public API.
The plan said R1 simulates 10^7 ticks in the normal test; the normal run does 10^6 (43 minutes at 120 BPM) and the 10^7 run is an ignored soak, for speed in debug.

title: Independent review of step 1 (#14) and PR 4a (#16): one real defect in 4a, found and fixed
zone: crates/octocore (src/steps.rs, src/engine.rs tests, tests/o4_steps.rs, tests/o4_guards.rs), handoffs/evidence, journal
why_risk: the defect was latent (no host can set a multiplier); the fix keeps every constant-multiplier result and changes only how a change of multiplier carries the phase
spec_rev: SPEC-0001 r3, release plan revision 2, section 2.7
evidence: Finding 1 (medium, verified by the reviewer by running code): the first 4a clock rounded the carried phase down to the new numerator's unit at every change of multiplier, always late. A chain of track 9 at x5 and member 8 at x1 (16 steps each) changes rate every 16 steps and ran 73 steps short in 200,000 ticks (27,708 against 27,781, 0.26 %); the f32 code did not drift. The plan's 'loses less than one unit per change' was true and was not enough: repeated changes add up, and the claims 'exact at any tick count' and 'nothing grows with time' held only for a constant multiplier.

Fix: the phase is kept as an exact reduced fraction of a tick and the unit is the smallest multiple of the new numerator that holds it (StepClock::retune); only past 2^80 does it round, once. Tests: R1e (the point in the step is exactly preserved), R1f (12 runs of 300,000 ticks with random changes agree with an exact reference on every tick), the reviewer's case (27,781 steps), an engine-level chain test that fails on the parent engine (o4-4a-red.txt part 3), an engine-level hyperstep link/unlink test, the smallest-unit test, the 2^80 fallback tests.

Finding 2 (medium, verified): nothing tested the engine path (chain-base switching, hyperstep link then unlink). The reviewer changed base_track to track at engine.rs:910 and the workspace still passed. The chain test now catches it (mutant SM17).

Finding 3 (low, verified): restoring a zero numerator: the f32 code went on counting and fired a burst (91 steps in a row) on the way out; the new clock freezes the phase. Deliberate, now listed and tested.

Finding 4 (low, verified): G1's mean was printed and not asserted; a +1 sample shift stayed inside max 1.05 and sigma 0.3 (the evidence's 'G1 catches OM5' was accidental). Added a mean fence of -0.6 to +0.05 (passes on the unchanged engine: means -0.501 to 0.000). It now catches OM5, OM7 and the new OM12 through the mean. The sigma fence is deterministic for the fixed runs and noisy for others; the test comment says so. The '1.02 samples' comment is corrected to the measured 0.995.

Finding 5 (low): corrected a false comment (20,000 ticks does expose all 49 wrong multipliers), the r1c name (it starts at the phase of tick N, it does not run N ticks), o4_steps.rs now reads the tick length from the engine's constants, STATE.md wording, the evidence README table, and 'ticks counted from 1' now says 'from a fresh or reset engine'. StepClock::at with a zero unit no longer divides by zero.

Reviewer's checks that found nothing: overflow (a 30-million-tick fuzz with random rate changes, maximum phase 341,644, no overflow), reset behaviour, den = 0, step of a tick or less, zone and cross-zone notes, G4.
unresolved: The independent reviews are fresh subagent sessions, not a human or another team: evidence, not a substitute for the owner's review.
The reviewer measured, and I did not, that a Stop then Play keeps the step phase (as the f32 code did); the comment now says 'fresh or reset engine'.
